1) the process of proton exchange between H(2)O and the H(n)PO(n)(3-n) anions is very fast, 2) H(n)PO3(n)(3-n)-O(-) moieties in water are responsible for a significant perturbation of the H-bond network, and 3) the flexibility of the first hydration shells of the phosphate anions increases with the increasing degree of protonation.

the process of dehydrogenation from H(n) PO4(3-n), n=0-3, in water is very fast and occurs through a concerted mechanism, and the hydrogen transfer process is strongly affected by the hydrogenation of the phosphate species.

the hydrogen transfer from the orthophosphates to water molecules occurs through a concerted mechanism, that the hydrogenated orthophosphate species have a significant effect upon the structure of the water molecules around them, and that the hydrogenation of the phosphate anions results in a decrease of the strength of the hydrogen bonds of the first hydration shells of the orthophos-phates.

the hydrogenation and hydration properties of the orthophos-phate anions and the proton transfer process between the orthophosphate ions and the surrounding water, which is important in the study of the phosphate chemistry and in the development of a better understanding of the phosphate chemistry in the aqueous phase.

a fundamental understanding of the hydrogen transfer mechanism in the aqueous solutions of H(n)OPO(4)(4-n) species and the effect of the phosphate anions on the structure of the surrounding water molecules.

the structural and dynamical properties of the orthophospate ions in water, with a focus on the hydrogen transfer process from the phosphate ions to the surrounding water and on the intermolecular and hydrogen-bonding properties of the phosphate-water systems.

the presence of phosphate species in water induces the formation of a new H-bonded network, which is characterized by the existence of H-H H-bonds and a more flexible first hydration shell.
